unit.why: A footnote (הערה) on R. Zvi Hirsh of Zhidachov tells an anecdote about his little brother's death on Pesach, then lists bibliographic references to his works.
unit.boundary_note: footnote attached to the biography of R. Zvi Hirsh in the previous division; the trailing list of works is bibliographic, not narrative

stories.start_quote: הערה מקובל כי הי' להם עוד
stories.summary_en: On Pesach a small brother of R. Zvi Hirsh of Zhidachov cried for leavened bread; when their mother asked him what to do, the tsaddik, absorbed in prayer, answered in Yiddish that a child who wants chametz on Pesach is not needed, and the child died at once.

quotes: הי' להם עוד את אחד ילד קטן
והלכה אמו לשאול פי בנה הגדול
tags.why: The tsaddik's little brother and his mother are the characters.

quotes: והלכה אמו לשאול פי בנה הגדול
tags.why: The mother acts by bringing the question to the tsaddik.
The story is set on Pesach.
The tsaddik is in the middle of praying.
He answers while rapt in holy fervor.
The burning fervor (להב) of his prayer is depicted.
The child's craving is for chametz, which is forbidden on Pesach.
The mother asks a question of law about feeding chametz to a child on Pesach.
The tsaddik's word takes effect supernaturally and kills the child.

missing_concepts: power of a tsaddik's unintended word or curse (שגגה היוצאת מלפני השליט)
